title: wtsi-hgi/hlarnaseq pipeline parameters
description: Precise analysis of human HLA RNASeq data by usign personalized references

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

rna_samples.description: Path to the RNA samplesheet containing indexed BAMs and paired unaligned reads.
rna_samples.help_text: Required top-level input: RNA-seq HLA quantification is what this pipeline does, so every stage runs off it. CSV file with the exact columns rna_id,bam,bai,unpaired_r1,unpaired_r2. See [usage docs](docs/usage.md#rna-samplesheet-input).

hla_region.description: Genomic region from which to extract complete read pairs.
hla_region.help_text: A samtools region string such as chr6:28500000-33400000. It is passed unchanged; chromosome notation must match the input BAM headers.

wgs_samples.description: Path to comma-separated file containing WGS BAM and BAI files.
wgs_samples.help_text: Optional WGS samplesheet with the exact columns WGS_sample_id,WGS_BAM_path,WGS_BAI_path. All entries are mandatory. See [usage docs](docs/usage.md#wgs-samplesheet-input).

array_samples.description: Path to a comma-separated file describing the SNP-array (PLINK) datasets used for HIBAG HLA calling.
array_samples.help_text: Alternative to --wgs_samples: genotype-side HLA alleles are called from SNP arrays with HIBAG instead of from WGS with HLA-LA. The two are mutually exclusive. Each row is one PLINK dataset, not one sample - a fileset may hold many samples and HIBAG predicts all of them at once. The sample IDs used downstream come from the .fam IID column and must match wgs_sample_id in --sample_key. Requires --hibag_model.

sample_key.description: Path to comma-separated file mapping RNA samples to their matched WGS sample.
sample_key.help_text: Required top-level input, with the exact columns rnaseq_sample_id,wgs_sample_id. One row per RNA sample with a matched WGS sample; RNA samples absent from this file (or when the file has zero data rows) are routed through the existing `RNA_ONLY:<rna_id>` consensus fallback path instead of being paired to a WGS sample. See [usage docs](docs/usage.md#rnawgs-sample-key-input).

rna_excluded_samples.description: Path to a plain-text file listing RNA sample IDs (one per line) to exclude from HLA consensus calling.
rna_excluded_samples.help_text: Optional. Passed through to the HLA_CONSENSUS step's `--rna-excluded-samples` flag.

wgs_excluded_samples.description: Path to a plain-text file listing WGS sample IDs (one per line) to exclude from HLA consensus calling.
wgs_excluded_samples.help_text: Optional. Passed through to the HLA_CONSENSUS step's `--wgs-excluded-samples` flag.

hla_consensus_truncate_fields.description: Number of colon-separated fields to keep when truncating HLA allele resolution during consensus calling.
hla_consensus_truncate_fields.help_text: Passed through to the HLA_CONSENSUS step's `--truncate-fields` flag.

hlapm_allowed_loci.description: Comma-separated allow-list of HLA loci (without the 'HLA-' prefix) to include when building HLApm personalized-reference input.
hlapm_allowed_loci.help_text: Passed through to the HLAPM_PREPARE_INPUT step's `--allowed-loci` flag. HLA_CONSENSUS output loci not in this list (e.g. `HLA-DRB3`, `HLA-H`, `HLA-J`, `HLA-K`, `HLA-L`) are silently omitted from the per-individual HLApm input TSVs, since HLApm's own per-allele locus regex cannot safely handle them.

hlapm_quantify_max_edit_distance.description: Maximum summed-mate edit distance (NM) for a read to count toward a gene's HLA read count.
hlapm_quantify_max_edit_distance.help_text: Passed through to the HLAPM_SUMMARIZE_READCOUNTS step and, as the same edit-distance threshold, to the HLA_READCOUNT_RECONCILE_DIFF step (HLA read-count reconciliation diff table). Matches the source script's hardcoded best_map_dist_threshold, based on "4 reads/100bp, as mapped in the original HGI pipeline".

rnaseq_strandedness.description: Library strandedness of the RNA-seq data, used by whole-genome featureCounts.
rnaseq_strandedness.help_text: Pipeline-wide (not per-sample) value merged into each RNA sample's meta map immediately before running SUBREAD_FEATURECOUNTS, which reads meta.strandedness directly. Not exposed as a --rna_samples samplesheet column in this iteration.

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

email.help_text: Set this parameter to your e-mail address to get a summary e-mail with details of the run sent to you when the workflow exits. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`) then you don't need to specify this on the command line for every run.

reference_genome_options.title: Reference genome options
reference_genome_options.description: Reference genome related files and options required for the workflow.

genome.help_text:
If using a reference genome configured in the pipeline using iGenomes, use this parameter to give the ID for the reference. This is then used to build the full paths for all required reference genome files e.g. `--genome GRCh38`. 

See the [nf-core website docs](https://nf-co.re/usage/reference_genomes) for more details.

fasta.help_text: This parameter is *mandatory* if `--genome` is not specified. If you don't have a BWA index available this will be generated for you automatically. Combine with `--save_reference` to save BWA index for future runs.

hlala_graph.help_text: Graph name to use for WGS HLA typing with HLA-LA. The default matches the standard GRCh38 graph used by the standalone prototype scripts.

hlala_graph_dir.description: Path to the prepared HLA-LA graph parent directory.
hlala_graph_dir.help_text: Required when `--wgs_samples` is provided. This path is passed to `HLA-LA.pl --customGraphDir` and must contain the prepared graph selected with `--hlala_graph`.

hibag_model.description: Path to a pre-fit HIBAG model file (.RData) used to impute HLA alleles from SNP-array genotypes.
hibag_model.help_text: Required with --array_samples. The file must contain either a single hlaAttrBagObj or a named list of hlaAttrBagObj, one per HLA locus - the shape the published HIBAG per-platform models use. Choose a model built for your array platform and genome assembly.

hibag_match_type.description: How HIBAG matches model SNPs to the array genotypes.
hibag_match_type.help_text: Passed to HIBAG::hlaPredict(). The default is strict and correct when the model was built against the same manifest and assembly as the data. If the run fails reporting that no model SNPs match, the error lists how many SNPs each criterion would find - 'RefSNP' is the most forgiving and is the usual fix for a model whose coordinates are offset from your manifest.

hibag_assembly.description: Genome assembly of the SNP-array genotypes, passed to HIBAG::hlaBED2Geno().
hibag_assembly.help_text: Must match the assembly the pre-fit model was built on. Published HIBAG models are commonly hg19, as are most Illumina array manifests.

hibag_loci.description: Optional comma-separated subset of HLA loci to predict, e.g. 'A,B,C'.
hibag_loci.help_text: Defaults to every locus present in --hibag_model. Requesting a locus the model file does not provide is an error.

hibag_min_prob.description: Drop HIBAG calls whose posterior probability is below this value.
hibag_min_prob.help_text: Defaults to 0, i.e. no filtering, matching the HLA-LA path which applies no confidence filter either. Raise it to discard low-confidence imputations before consensus calling.

hibag_min_matched_snps.description: Minimum fraction of a locus's model SNPs that must be found in the array data before HIBAG will impute that locus.
hibag_min_matched_snps.help_text: Guards against silently wrong calls. HIBAG does not fail on poor SNP overlap - it returns confident-looking but unreliable alleles - so this check fails the run instead, reporting how many SNPs each --hibag_match_type criterion would find and which to switch to. Set to 0 to disable, only if you accept unreliable calls.

hlapm_repo.description: Path to a local, pre-cloned checkout of the HLApm repository (https://github.com/davenportlab/HLApm). Optional under a container profile; required without one.
hlapm_repo.help_text: This path is used as `HLAPM_HOME` when running HLApm's `bulkRNA_build_personalized_HLA_ref()`. Under `-profile docker`/`singularity`/`apptainer`, `HLAPM_BUILD_REF`'s image already contains HLApm at a pinned commit (build it once with `scripts/build_image_hlapm.sh`), so this parameter is only needed to override that baked-in copy with a patched or newer checkout. Without a container engine (`-profile conda`, or no profile), HLApm cannot be provisioned automatically - Conda can install its R dependencies but not a git checkout - so this parameter is mandatory. The pipeline never clones or fetches HLApm at runtime; any checkout passed here (including its bundled reference data) must be prepared by the operator beforehand.

gtf.description: Path to the whole-genome reference GTF used for per-sample featureCounts quantification.
gtf.help_text: Required. Passed to SUBREAD_FEATURECOUNTS as the annotation file run once per RNA sample against that sample's existing whole-genome, coordinate-sorted BAM (`--rna_samples`'s `bam`/`bai` columns), producing a per-sample whole-genome gene-count table. This is distinct from HLApm's per-allele GTFs, which cover only genotyped HLA alleles.

arcashla_genes.description: Comma-separated gene list passed to `arcasHLA genotype -g`.
arcashla_genes.help_text: Genes are intersected with those known to the reference pointed to by `--arcashla_reference_dir`; unrecognised gene names are silently dropped by arcasHLA as long as at least one requested gene is valid.

arcashla_reference_dir.description: Path to a pre-built arcasHLA reference directory (IMGT/HLA + kallisto index).
arcashla_reference_dir.help_text: Required. arcasHLA has no option to point `genotype` at an external reference at runtime, so `ARCASHLA_GENOTYPE` takes this directory as a staged process input (which is what makes container engines bind-mount it automatically) and symlinks it into place as its own `dat/ref` at task start. It may therefore live on any filesystem the executor can read, with no manual bind flags. Build it once with `scripts/build_arcashla_reference.sh`; the pipeline checks at launch that the directory really contains a built reference (`hla.idx`, `hla.p.json`), not just that it exists.

igenomes_ignore.description: Do not load the iGenomes reference config.
igenomes_ignore.help_text: Do not load `igenomes.config` when running the pipeline. You may choose this option if you observe clashes between custom parameters and those supplied in `igenomes.config`.

igenomes_base.description: The base path to the igenomes reference files

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

hook_url.description: Incoming hook URL for messaging service
hook_url.help_text: Incoming hook URL for messaging service. Currently, MS Teams and Slack are supported.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

pipelines_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of pipeline test dataset files

trace_report_suffix.description: Suffix to add to the trace report filename. Default is the date and time in the format yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss.

help_full.description: Display the full detailed help message.

show_hidden.description: Display hidden parameters in the help message (only works when --help or --help_full are provided).
